subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled session-memory filenames and `# Session` headers use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` instead of the host or `TZ` timezone?
rationale: The technical gap is clear, but the change would alter shipped memory artifact naming/header semantics for users whose configured timezone differs from the gateway host timezone.

options.title: Adopt userTimezone for session-memory
options.body: Align slugged session-memory artifacts with auto-flush and system prompt time by reusing configured-timezone helpers, with focused upgrade-aware tests and docs.

options.title: Keep host-local session-memory
options.body: Document that `userTimezone` affects prompts and auto-flush but not bundled session-memory filenames/headers, preserving current shipped file naming behavior.

options.title: Add explicit memory timezone setting
options.body: Create a dedicated memory artifact timezone knob only if maintainers want separate semantics and accept the extra config surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt userTimezone for session-memory
recommendation.body: Align slugged session-memory artifacts with auto-flush and system prompt time by reusing configured-timezone helpers, with focused upgrade-aware tests and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is tied to the current session-memory timezone implementation and the merged scoped repair that set host-local behavior.
